insightTypes.label: Feature request
insightTypes.definition: The customer asks for a capability Invoca does not have today, or for an existing one to work differently.
examples: "Can we build our own QM scorecard criteria for disclosure language?"
"We need to push dashboards into Looker without a CSV step."
counterExamples: Something that should already work but is broken is a bug.
A request for training or a how-to answer is not a feature request.

insightTypes.label: Bug / defect
insightTypes.definition: An Invoca product or integration behaves incorrectly, loses data, is late, or contradicts its documented behaviour.
examples: "Offline conversions land in Google Ads two to three days late."
"PreSense data disappears when Genesys transfers the call."
counterExamples: A complaint about a rep, a slow support reply or a missed meeting is not a product bug.
Problems in the customer's own systems with no Invoca component are not bugs.

insightTypes.label: Pricing objection
insightTypes.definition: Pushback on price, packaging, add-ons, contract terms or perceived value for money.
examples: "Finance wants to know why PreSense is an add-on. It feels like paying twice."
counterExamples: A competitor quoting a lower price is a competitor mention; log both only if the customer also objects to Invoca's price.
A billing error (wrong invoice) is a bug in billing, not an objection.

insightTypes.label: Competitor mention
insightTypes.definition: A named competitor is being evaluated, is pitching, or is used as a comparison (CallRail, Marchex, CallTrackingMetrics, WhatConverts, Gong).
examples: "CallRail is telling Jeff they sync conversions the same day."
counterExamples: Mentioning a partner Invoca integrates with (Salesforce, Genesys, Five9) is not a competitor mention.

insightTypes.label: Churn risk
insightTypes.definition: Signals that the customer may not renew, may reduce scope, or is actively considering leaving. Hedged threats count.
examples: "If this isn't fixed by renewal we'll have to look around."
counterExamples: Routine budget planning with no threat to the relationship is not churn risk.
Frustration about one bug, with no link to renewal or scope, is the bug alone.

insightTypes.label: Praise
insightTypes.definition: Specific positive feedback about an Invoca capability or outcome that a product team would want to hear.
examples: "Our dispatchers love the AI call summaries."
counterExamples: Politeness ("thanks, great call") is not praise.
Praise for the CSM personally, with no product angle, is not routed.

productAreas.label: Call Tracking & Attribution
productAreas.definition: Tracking numbers, dynamic number insertion (DNI), the Invoca tag, call flows, campaign and keyword attribution, Advanced IVR.
examples: DNI numbers not swapping on a single-page checkout.
Calls attributed to the wrong campaign.
counterExamples: Conversions arriving late in Google Ads are integrations, not attribution.

productAreas.label: Signal AI
productAreas.definition: Signal AI Studio and Discovery: call classification, custom signals, spam detection, transcription, summaries, redaction.
examples: After-hours callers tagged as spam.
Transcripts not redacting a spoken date of birth.
counterExamples: Scorecards for agent coaching belong to Quality Management.

productAreas.label: PreSense
productAreas.definition: Passing a caller's digital journey to contact-center agents and routing before the call is answered.
examples: Screen pop arrives blank after a Genesys transfer.
counterExamples: The Genesys connector failing for all call data is integrations.

productAreas.label: Integrations
productAreas.definition: Data flowing between Invoca and partner platforms: Google Ads, Meta, Adobe Analytics, Marketo, Salesforce, Five9, Genesys, NICE, Amazon Connect.
examples: Offline conversions late to Google Ads.
Salesforce field mapping breaking on custom objects.
counterExamples: A missing PreSense field on transfer is PreSense, even when the platform is Genesys.

productAreas.label: Quality Management
productAreas.definition: AI-Powered Quality Management: automated scorecards, agent evaluation, coaching and compliance checks on 100% of calls.
examples: Custom scorecard criteria for required disclosures.
counterExamples: A spam label on a call is Signal AI.

productAreas.label: AI Agents
productAreas.definition: AI Voice Agent and AI Messaging Agent: automated answering, intake, SMS follow-up and handoff to live agents.
examples: Voice Agent transfers to a live agent without the caller's context.
counterExamples: Human agents' call handling quality is Quality Management.

productAreas.label: Billing & Pricing
productAreas.definition: Contracts, packaging, add-ons, seat and usage pricing, invoices and renewal terms.
examples: PreSense sold as an add-on at renewal.
Per-rooftop pricing versus a competitor.
counterExamples: A reporting export limitation is platform even when raised in a renewal call.

productAreas.label: Platform & Reporting
productAreas.definition: Reporting, dashboards, exports, UI, permissions, user management and anything not covered elsewhere.
examples: Exporting dashboards to Looker or Google Sheets on a schedule.
counterExamples: Problems inside a partner integration belong to integrations.

severities.label: Low
severities.definition: Nice to have, cosmetic, or a single user's preference. No revenue impact.

severities.label: Medium
severities.definition: A real workflow cost or a recurring annoyance; a workaround exists.

severities.label: High
severities.definition: Material business impact (spend, bidding, compliance, renewal) or no workaround.

severities.label: Critical
severities.definition: Outage, data loss, a compliance exposure in progress, or an immediate threat to the account.
